nodes.name: StatisticalMethod
nodes.definition: A procedure for describing data or making inferences under explicit assumptions about variation, sampling, and a target of interpretation.

nodes.name: ProbabilityDistribution
nodes.definition: A mathematical specification assigning probabilities to measurable outcomes under a stated sample space and event structure.

nodes.name: ProbabilityValue
nodes.definition: A numerical measure of an event's uncertainty or frequency under a specified probability model, constrained to the unit interval.

nodes.name: RandomVariable
nodes.definition: A measurable mapping from a probability space's outcomes to a specified value space.

nodes.name: SampleSpace
nodes.definition: The set of possible elementary outcomes represented by a specified probability model.

nodes.name: ProbabilityEvent
nodes.definition: A measurable subset of a probability model's sample space to which a probability can be assigned.
examples: The set of die outcomes greater than four
counterexamples: The physical act of rolling a die

nodes.name: ProbabilityModel
nodes.definition: A mathematical specification of possible outcomes and probabilities used to represent uncertainty for a stated purpose.

nodes.name: ConditionalProbability
nodes.definition: A probability assigned to an event conditional on specified information or another event under a probability model.

nodes.name: JointDistribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution over a collection of jointly modeled random variables.

nodes.name: MarginalDistribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution of a subset of jointly modeled variables obtained without conditioning on the remaining variables.

nodes.name: ConditionalDistribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution of variables conditional on specified values or information about other variables.

nodes.name: DiscreteDistribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution concentrated on a finite or countably infinite set of possible values.

nodes.name: AbsolutelyContinuousDistribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution representable by a density with respect to the specified continuous reference measure.

nodes.name: BernoulliDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution over two outcomes parameterized by the probability of one designated outcome.

nodes.name: BinomialDistribution
nodes.definition: The distribution of a count of designated outcomes in a fixed number of independent Bernoulli trials with a common success probability.

nodes.name: CategoricalDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution assigning probabilities to one outcome from a finite set of categories.

nodes.name: MultinomialDistribution
nodes.definition: The distribution of category counts from a fixed number of independent categorical trials sharing category probabilities.

nodes.name: PoissonDistribution
nodes.definition: A count distribution whose probability mass at a nonnegative integer is determined by a positive rate parameter through the Poisson mass function.

nodes.name: GeometricDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution of trials or failures until the first designated outcome in independent Bernoulli trials, with the counting convention stated explicitly.

nodes.name: NegativeBinomialDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution of failures or trials before a specified number of designated Bernoulli outcomes, with parameterization and counting convention stated explicitly.

nodes.name: DiscreteUniformDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution assigning equal probability to each member of a specified finite outcome set.

nodes.name: NormalDistribution
nodes.definition: An absolutely continuous distribution on the real line with density proportional to the exponential of a negative squared standardized deviation, parameterized by mean and positive variance.

nodes.name: LogNormalDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution of a positive random variable whose logarithm follows a specified normal distribution.

nodes.name: ContinuousUniformDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution with constant probability density over a specified bounded interval and zero density outside it.

nodes.name: ExponentialDistribution
nodes.definition: A nonnegative continuous distribution with constant hazard under its standard positive rate parameterization.

nodes.name: GammaDistribution
nodes.definition: A positive continuous distribution in the gamma family, with shape and rate or scale parameterization explicitly identified.

nodes.name: BetaDistribution
nodes.definition: A continuous distribution on the unit interval whose density is determined by two positive shape parameters.

nodes.name: StudentTDistribution
nodes.definition: A continuous distribution defined by a standard normal variable divided by the square root of an independent scaled chi-squared variable.

nodes.name: ChiSquaredDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution of the sum of squares of a specified number of independent standard normal variables.

nodes.name: FDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution of the ratio of two independent chi-squared variables each divided by its degrees of freedom.

nodes.name: MixtureDistribution
nodes.definition: A probability distribution formed by weighting component distributions according to a mixing distribution.

nodes.name: EmpiricalDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution assigning probability mass to observed sample values according to a specified empirical weighting rule.

nodes.name: StatisticalPopulation
nodes.definition: The collection of units or outcomes about which a statistical description or inference is intended.

nodes.name: StatisticalSample
nodes.definition: An information representation of observations selected from a target population under a stated sampling procedure; repeated observations remain distinguishable.
examples: Recorded measurements of the selected study participants
counterexamples: The physical group of participants independently of its recorded observations

nodes.name: Dataset
nodes.definition: An organized collection of recorded values with a stated structure, observation unit, and interpretation.

nodes.name: DataRecord
nodes.definition: A structured information unit recording values associated with an identified observation, entity, or event.

nodes.name: StatisticalVariable
nodes.definition: A defined characteristic whose values are recorded or modeled for observational units.

nodes.name: CategoricalVariable
nodes.definition: A statistical variable whose values identify categories under a specified category scheme.

nodes.name: OrdinalVariable
nodes.definition: A categorical variable whose categories carry an ordering without requiring meaningful numerical distances.

nodes.name: QuantitativeVariable
nodes.definition: A statistical variable with numerical values interpreted through a defined quantitative scale.

nodes.name: MeasurementScale
nodes.definition: A specification of how observed values represent a characteristic and which comparisons or transformations preserve its meaning.

nodes.name: Statistic
nodes.definition: A quantity or structured value calculated from a sample according to a specified rule, distinguished from an unknown population parameter.

nodes.name: StatisticalParameter
nodes.definition: A quantity or structured value specifying a property of a probability model or target population.

nodes.name: Estimator
nodes.definition: A rule mapping possible samples to estimates of a specified population or model quantity.

nodes.name: StatisticalEstimate
nodes.definition: The value obtained by applying an estimator to observed data under a specified analysis.

nodes.name: SampleMean
nodes.definition: The arithmetic average of sample values under an explicitly stated weighting convention.

nodes.name: SampleMedian
nodes.definition: A sample location statistic dividing ordered observations into lower and upper portions under a stated convention for ties and even sample size.

nodes.name: SampleVariance
nodes.definition: A statistic measuring average squared deviations from a sample location, with denominator and weighting convention stated explicitly.

nodes.name: StandardDeviation
nodes.definition: The nonnegative square root of a specified variance, expressed in the original value units.

nodes.name: Quantile
nodes.definition: A threshold associated with a specified cumulative probability or sample fraction, with the quantile convention identified.

nodes.name: Expectation
nodes.definition: The probability-weighted mean of a random variable under a specified distribution when the expectation is defined.

nodes.name: Covariance
nodes.definition: The expected product of centered values of two variables under a specified joint distribution when defined.

nodes.name: CorrelationCoefficient
nodes.definition: A numerical measure of association between variables under a specified correlation definition.
counterexamples: A proof that changing one variable causes the other

nodes.name: InformationEntropy
nodes.definition: A functional of a probability distribution measuring uncertainty under a specified entropy definition, logarithm base, and reference measure.

nodes.name: MutualInformation
nodes.definition: A measure of statistical dependence defined by the divergence between a joint distribution and the product of its marginals.

nodes.name: LikelihoodFunction
nodes.definition: A function of model parameters proportional to the probability mass or density of the observed data under the model.
examples: Likelihood of parameters for fixed observed data
counterexamples: Posterior probability of parameters without a prior

nodes.name: PriorDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution representing uncertainty about model quantities before incorporating a designated observation through the specified update.

nodes.name: PosteriorDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution representing uncertainty after conditioning a prior model on designated observations through a specified likelihood.

nodes.name: PosteriorPredictiveDistribution
nodes.definition: A distribution of future or replicated observations obtained by integrating a sampling model over a posterior distribution.

nodes.name: CredibleInterval
nodes.definition: An interval containing a specified posterior probability for a quantity under a Bayesian model and interval selection rule.
examples: An interval with 95 percent posterior mass
counterexamples: A claim of repeated-sampling coverage without a separate argument

nodes.name: ConfidenceInterval
nodes.definition: An interval produced by a procedure with a stated repeated-sampling coverage property under specified assumptions.
examples: An interval from a procedure with nominal 95 percent coverage
counterexamples: A statement that a fixed parameter has 95 percent posterior probability without a Bayesian model

nodes.name: PredictionInterval
nodes.definition: An interval intended to cover a future observation under a specified prediction model and coverage interpretation.

nodes.name: StandardError
nodes.definition: The standard deviation or estimated standard deviation of an estimator's sampling distribution under a specified design.

nodes.name: SamplingMethod
nodes.definition: A statistical method selecting observational units from a target population under an explicit selection mechanism.

nodes.name: ProbabilitySampling
nodes.definition: A sampling method assigning units known or specified selection probabilities through a random mechanism.

nodes.name: StratifiedSampling
nodes.definition: Probability sampling carried out separately within defined population strata and combined under a stated weighting design.

nodes.name: ClusterSampling
nodes.definition: Probability sampling selecting groups of units as sampling units at one or more stages.

nodes.name: ConvenienceSampling
nodes.definition: A sampling method selecting units based primarily on accessibility rather than a specified probability design.

nodes.name: EstimationMethod
nodes.definition: A statistical method producing estimates of specified model or population quantities from observations.

nodes.name: MaximumLikelihoodEstimation
nodes.definition: An estimation method selecting parameter values that maximize the likelihood of observed data within a specified model.

nodes.name: BayesianInference
nodes.definition: A statistical method conditioning a probability model on observations to revise uncertainty over quantities of interest.

nodes.name: BootstrapResampling
nodes.definition: A statistical method approximating an estimator's behavior by repeatedly resampling observations or fitted-model realizations under a stated resampling design.

nodes.name: PermutationMethod
nodes.definition: A statistical method evaluating a statistic under rearrangements justified by an exchangeability or randomization assumption.

nodes.name: MonteCarloMethod
nodes.definition: A statistical method approximating a quantity through random simulation under a specified sampling model.

nodes.name: MarkovChainMonteCarlo
nodes.definition: A Monte Carlo method using a Markov chain designed to have a target distribution as a stationary distribution.

nodes.name: HypothesisTest
nodes.definition: A statistical method evaluating a null hypothesis through a statistic and a rejection or evidence rule with specified assumptions.

nodes.name: PairedStatisticalTest
nodes.definition: A hypothesis test accounting for paired observations or matched experimental units in its comparison.

nodes.name: TTest
nodes.definition: A hypothesis test using a Student-t reference distribution under assumptions appropriate to its mean-comparison design.

nodes.name: ChiSquaredTest
nodes.definition: A hypothesis test using a chi-squared reference distribution under the specified count or variance-model assumptions.

nodes.name: MultipleTestingMethod
nodes.definition: A statistical method addressing an error criterion across a specified family of hypothesis tests.

nodes.name: NullHypothesis
nodes.definition: A proposition designated as the reference claim for a specified statistical test.

nodes.name: AlternativeHypothesis
nodes.definition: A proposition or set of possibilities evaluated against the designated null in a statistical test.

nodes.name: PValue
nodes.definition: A probability under a specified null model of results at least as incompatible with that model as the observed statistic according to the test's ordering.
examples: A tail probability under the null model
counterexamples: The probability that the null hypothesis is true

nodes.name: SignificanceLevel
nodes.definition: A bound or target for a test procedure's type-I error probability under its null assumptions.

nodes.name: StatisticalPower
nodes.definition: The probability that a test rejects its null under a specified alternative effect, design, and decision rule.

nodes.name: EffectSize
nodes.definition: A quantity representing the magnitude of a specified difference, association, or intervention effect on a defined scale.

nodes.name: PracticalSignificance
nodes.definition: A property of an estimated effect being consequential relative to specified decision costs, benefits, or domain thresholds.

nodes.name: RegressionAnalysis
nodes.definition: A statistical method relating a response to explanatory variables under a specified conditional model and interpretation.

nodes.name: LinearRegressionAnalysis
nodes.definition: Regression analysis using a response model linear in its specified coefficients, with error assumptions stated separately.

nodes.name: LogisticRegressionAnalysis
nodes.definition: Regression analysis using a logistic link for a modeled binary response probability or a stated extension.

nodes.name: TimeSeriesAnalysis
nodes.definition: A statistical method for observations ordered in time that explicitly addresses their temporal structure.

nodes.name: SurvivalAnalysis
nodes.definition: A statistical method analyzing time to events while accounting for the stated censoring and observation process.

nodes.name: MetaAnalysis
nodes.definition: A statistical method combining estimates or evidence across studies under an explicit model of comparability and dependence.

nodes.name: SensitivityAnalysis
nodes.definition: A statistical method examining how conclusions vary under changes in assumptions, inputs, or analysis choices.

nodes.name: CausalInference
nodes.definition: A statistical method estimating or assessing intervention-related effects under an explicit causal model and identification assumptions.

nodes.name: ExperimentDesign
nodes.definition: A specification of experimental units, interventions, assignment, measurements, and analysis intended to address a research question.

nodes.name: RandomizedExperimentDesign
nodes.definition: An experiment design assigning interventions through a specified random mechanism.

nodes.name: ControlledExperimentDesign
nodes.definition: An experiment design comparing intervention conditions with one or more defined control conditions.

nodes.name: PairedExperimentDesign
nodes.definition: An experiment design linking observations through the same unit or a declared matching rule for comparison.

nodes.name: FactorialExperimentDesign
nodes.definition: An experiment design varying combinations of levels of multiple factors to examine their effects and interactions.

nodes.name: ObservationalStudy
nodes.definition: An intentional study observing variables without assigning the exposure or intervention whose effect is at issue.

nodes.name: StatisticalExperiment
nodes.definition: An intentional study assigning or manipulating conditions according to a design and recording relevant outcomes.

nodes.name: Confounding
nodes.definition: A property of a causal comparison in which the observed association is mixed with effects of other causes under the assumed causal structure.

nodes.name: SelectionBias
nodes.definition: A systematic distortion arising from how units or observations enter or remain in the analyzed sample relative to the target inference.

nodes.name: MeasurementBias
nodes.definition: A systematic distortion introduced by a measurement process relative to the intended measured quantity.

nodes.name: PublicationBias
nodes.definition: A systematic distortion in available study evidence caused by selective dissemination related to results or other inference-relevant features.

nodes.name: MissingDataState
nodes.definition: A condition in which values intended for an observation or analysis are unavailable, with the missingness mechanism treated separately.

nodes.name: ImputationMethod
nodes.definition: A statistical method supplying modeled or selected substitute values for missing observations under explicit assumptions.

nodes.name: StatisticalOutlierRole
nodes.definition: A contextual role of an observation judged unusually distant from an identified reference pattern or model.
examples: A measurement flagged relative to a specified distribution
counterexamples: An intrinsically erroneous datum merely because it is rare

nodes.name: StatisticalIndependenceCondition
nodes.definition: A condition specifying factorization of a joint probability law into relevant marginal laws under a stated model.
examples: Independent draws under a declared sampling model
counterexamples: Two reports that copied the same original source

nodes.name: ExchangeabilityCondition
nodes.definition: A condition that a specified joint distribution is invariant under the allowed permutations of observation indices.

nodes.name: StatisticalIdentifiability
nodes.definition: A property of a model or estimand being uniquely recoverable from the specified observable distribution and assumptions.

nodes.name: AleatoricUncertainty
nodes.definition: Uncertainty attributed to modeled outcome variability under a stated representation and information set.

nodes.name: EpistemicUncertainty
nodes.definition: Uncertainty attributed to limited knowledge about models, parameters, or relevant conditions under a stated representation.

nodes.name: EvidenceSourceRecord
nodes.definition: A record identifying the origin, content boundary, and relevant context of information used as evidence.

nodes.name: EvidenceItem
nodes.definition: An identifiable item of information considered as bearing on a proposition under an explicit relevance and source interpretation.

nodes.name: DirectObservation
nodes.definition: An observation process acquiring information through stated perception or measurement rather than solely by repeating another report.

nodes.name: ReportedObservation
nodes.definition: An information representation of an observation attributed to a reporting source whose access and reliability require separate assessment.

nodes.name: DerivedClaim
nodes.definition: A proposition asserted on the basis of other claims or observations through an identified inference procedure.

nodes.name: ClaimContradiction
nodes.definition: A specification that claims cannot jointly hold under the same meaning, scope, time, and background assumptions.

nodes.name: EvidenceRebuttal
nodes.definition: Information offered as a reason to reject or reduce support for a specified claim under an explicit interpretation.

nodes.name: IndependentSupportAssessment
nodes.definition: An assessment that specified evidential contributions provide nonduplicative support under a stated dependence model.

nodes.name: SourceDependenceAssessment
nodes.definition: An assessment of how evidential contributions share observations, sources, mechanisms, or derivation paths relevant to combining support.

nodes.name: BeliefAssessment
nodes.definition: A record of the assessed support or uncertainty of a specified proposition at a specified time, with evidence and method identified.

nodes.name: ConfidenceScore
nodes.definition: A numeric or ordered assessment of confidence whose target, scale, and calibration interpretation must be stated.
examples: A calibrated probability for a defined proposition
counterexamples: An arbitrary score silently interpreted as a probability

nodes.name: EvidenceWeight
nodes.definition: A method-dependent representation of an evidential contribution's influence on an assessment, distinguished from independent event counts.

nodes.name: LikelihoodRatio
nodes.definition: A ratio of likelihoods of the same observations under two specified models or hypotheses.

nodes.name: BayesFactor
nodes.definition: A ratio of marginal likelihoods of observed data under two specified probabilistic models, with their parameter priors included.

nodes.name: ProperScoringRule
nodes.definition: A probabilistic forecast scoring rule for which the expected score is optimized by reporting the forecaster's true distribution under the rule's assumptions.

nodes.name: BrierScore
nodes.definition: A mean squared discrepancy between stated event probabilities and realized event indicators under a specified aggregation convention.

nodes.name: LogarithmicScore
nodes.definition: A probabilistic forecast score based on the logarithm of probability or density assigned to the realized outcome, with sign and density conventions stated.

nodes.name: CalibrationCurve
nodes.definition: A representation comparing predicted probabilities or confidence levels with observed outcome frequencies under a stated grouping and evaluation design.

nodes.name: EvaluationIntent
nodes.definition: A distinct information need or task objective used as an evaluation unit; paraphrases of the same need remain one intent for dependence-aware analysis.
examples: Finding a compiler versus finding source code
counterexamples: Five paraphrases counted as five independent tasks

nodes.name: PairedRouteResult
nodes.definition: A record of baseline and candidate navigation outcomes for the same evaluation intent under matched conditions.

nodes.name: NavigationEvaluation
nodes.definition: A statistical method comparing retrieval or traversal outcomes over defined intents with controlled presentation, budget, and model conditions.
